rules.title: Massachusetts anti-discrimination law: public assistance and housing subsidy recipients (and protected-class tenant selection)
rules.requirement: Landlords and others offering rental accommodations may not discriminate against someone because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy such as a voucher, or because of a requirement of that program. Landlords also may not refuse to rent or ask about protected characteristics such as race, sex, age, marital status, veteran status or disability.
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient
rules.effective_date_note: The document does not give an effective date for subsection 10.
rules.key_value: ban on discrimination against public assistance / housing subsidy recipients

unverifiable_exemptions: Subsection 7 does not apply to leasing a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner lives in the other unit
Subsection 11 (children) has exemptions for small dwellings and owner-occupied two-family units

rules.exemptions: Subsection 7 excludes leasing a single apartment in a two-family dwelling occupied by the owner as a residence.

parsed.doc_summary: G.L. c. 151B § 4 (unlawful practices) is mostly about employment and general housing discrimination. The only in-scope provision is subsection 10, which bars discrimination against public assistance and housing subsidy recipients. It is captured as a screening_restrictions rule. The criminal-record limits in this section apply to employment only, not housing.
